record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: For house allocation via exchanges in a social network, determine the complexity and algorithmic structure of the model when exchanges are allowed to occur along cycles of length greater than 2, rather than only through swaps between two applicants.

evidence.quote: The most striking open question regarding exchanges in social networks involves longer cycles instead of swaps only.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following house allocation model on a social network. Let G=(V,E) be a simple undirected graph whose vertices V={1,...,n} represent applicants. Each applicant i initially owns a distinct house h_i and has a strict preference order ≻_i over the set H={h_1,...,h_n} of houses. Applicants may exchange houses only along cycles in G: for any simple cycle v_1, v_2, ..., v_k, v_1 in G (with k≥2), the applicants on the cycle may simultaneously rotate their currently held houses (each v_j passing its house to v_{j+1}, indices mod k), provided that every participating applicant strictly prefers the house they receive to the house they currently hold. An allocation is a permutation assigning each applicant a house; it is reachable from the initial endowment by a sequence of such cyclic exchanges.

The case k=2 (swaps along edges only) has been studied and its computational complexity is understood. The problem asks: when cyclic exchanges of arbitrary length k≥2 are permitted (with the cycle required to be a cycle in G), determine the computational complexity of the natural decision problems associated with this model — in particular, deciding whether a given target allocation is reachable from the initial endowment via a sequence of cyclic exchanges along cycles of G, deciding whether a Pareto-improving cyclic exchange exists, and computing a (core-)stable or Pareto-optimal reachable allocation. Provide algorithms or hardness results, and describe the algorithmic structure of the model.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2023–2024) studies housing markets on networks with mechanisms such as "Swap With Neighbors", "Leave and Share", and "Connected Trading Cycles", and establishes NP-hardness for several core-related questions and for swap-reachability on cliques and caterpillars. However, no source in the search resolves the general complexity and algorithmic structure of network-restricted exchanges along cycles of length greater than 2 in the house allocation setting; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Housing Market on Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes mechanisms (Swap With Neighbors, Leave and Share, Connected Trading Cycles) for housing markets where exchanges respect a network; does not settle full complexity for longer cycles.
status_evidence.claim: Cyclic exchanges on networks remain an active area of investigation.

status_evidence.title: The Computational Complexity of the Housing Market
status_evidence.snippet: Studies complexity of housing-market core problems; establishes NP-hardness for certain allocation decisions.
status_evidence.claim: Related complexity results exist but do not resolve the network-cyclic exchange model in general.
